title: Light Armored Reconnaissance Operations Chief (MGySgt to MSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O #
raw_text:
20. MOS 0393, Light Armored Reconnaissance Operations Chief (MGySgt to MSgt)
PMOS, DC PP&O #

    a. Summary. The Light Armored Reconnaissance Operations Chief (LAR Ops
chief) serves as the senior enlisted tactical advisor to the commander and
staff of a light armored reconnaissance (LAR) company or battalion. They
advise the commander in the tactical employment of the organic weapons
systems of the unit, the condition, care, and economical use of unit
resources and equipment. They coordinate and supervise all aspects of the
company or battalion combat operations center (COC) or administrative
logistics operations center (ALOC). They ensure that personnel are trained
and proficient in the employment of C4I systems and manages the flow of
information provided through them. They assist with the timely collection,
review, and distribution of orders, messages, briefs, reports, training
schedules and all tasks in support of the units core and assigned mission
essential tasks. The LAR Operations Chief advises and makes recommendations
for the planning, coordination, and execution of the units fire support plan.
They manage the 03XX personnel within the unit, in order to minimize crew
turbulence amongst formed and trained crews, assists with the development of
the units training plan, and managing the unit readiness program. They
coordinate and supervise the embarkation and debarkation of the unit. Master
Sergeants are assigned as battalion logistics chiefs, assistant battalion
operations chiefs, and headquarters & service company operations chiefs.



                                     3-42                        Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



Master Gunnery Sergeants are assigned as A/C and R/C battalion operations
chiefs, Marine Corps warfighting lab (MCWL) operations chief, Marine air
ground task force-training center (MAGTF-TC) operations chief, program
manager-light armored vehicle (PM-LAV) operations advisor, and plans,
policies, and operations (PP&O) LAR advocate/OccFld sponsor.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have WS-I water survival qualification.

            (2) Security requirement:   must be TS/SCI security eligible.

            (3) Must have held the PMOS 0363, Light Armored Reconnaissance Unit
Leader.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Successful completion of the GCE Operations Specialist Course
(N30RCC1 or N30KBC1) prior to being assigned the PMOS 0393.

        (2) 0393 MSgt’s and MGySgt’s must complete the Operations and Tactics
Instructor Chief Course (M09HE35).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (de), Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Training and Readiness
(T&R) Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) 55-1019 Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders.

            (2) First-Line Supervisor of Weapons Specialist/Crew Members 55-2012.

            (3) Infantry 55-3016.

            (4) Armored Assault Vehicle Crew Members 55-3013.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Light Armored Reconnaissance Marine, 0313.

            (2) Reconnaissance Marine, 0321.

            (3) Light Armored Reconnaissance Unit Leader, 0363.

            (4) Infantry Unit Leader, 0369.

            (5) Infantry Operations chief, 0399.

            (6) Operations and Tactics Instructor, 0577.

            (7) Ground Operations Specialist, 8711.

# When promoted to MSgt, the 0393 MOS will only be awarded after completing
the MOS requirements. To facilitate M&RA with assignments, Marines may be
assigned using the Intended MOS for which they were selected until they have
met the requirements.




                                          3-43                        Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
